approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It draws breeding sources from score bands, recombines connected fragments from two sources, and applies local atom, bond and ring edits. Ordinary mutation can continue for several steps, and a successful crossover can receive a finishing mutation. Stable canonical identity checks admit a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on the complete chronological archive of accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws choose the molecules that receive evaluation. Accepted offspring update both the predictor and the score-ranked breeding population. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Its bond-change primitive currently changes one existing bond's order; it has no coordinated, degree-preserving connectivity rearrangement.
approach.novelty: Add one optional two-single-bond rewiring move: cut two disjoint single bonds in one source and reconnect their four endpoints in a different matching, conserving the source atoms, each atom's heavy degree and bond-order sum, and the molecular formula. The move can reach a complete arrangement without requiring a valid sequence of separate one-edge changes. The first bond keeps its inherited random choice; only that selected bond gains an equally weighted choice between the old bond-order path and uniform eligible rewiring descriptors. Earlier siblings moved a pendant branch along an aromatic ring or assembled rings from two parents; neither supplied this single-source, degree-conserving neighborhood, and both lost endpoint score despite real downstream use. The ring-without-finishing combination also lost. This experiment retains ordinary continuation and the supported finishing branch. Conservation and wider connectivity are hypotheses about access, while actual accepted improvements, later use and the complete endpoint comparison determine whether that access helps.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is a missing coordinated connectivity neighborhood within the otherwise productive exchange-disabled Parent n-62daf219c70a, not a demonstrated causal penalty for any particular conserved motif. The actual three supplied summary.json and run.log files show all fifteen tasks successful, 4,350 accepted offspring, macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747; seed macros are 0.625411930168826, 0.560865654270234 and 0.600731364761313. The indexed full Parent activation audit records 629 strict best-parent beats, 258 incumbent improvements and 2,401 offspring later used as breeders, while the source's change_bond only changes one bond order. The new read-only audit .slots/round-0024-slot-0/plan_rewiring_opportunity_audit.json reads every actual Parent task log, excludes repeated emitted receipts, and recovers the selected bond from all 7,992 raw bond-order changes. Of those, 6,763 select a single bond; 6,653 have at least one structurally eligible degree-conserving descriptor under the registered predicate, totaling 112,693 physical descriptors across calls. Every task/seed has support. These are passive unconstructed descriptors: no rewiring was executed, sanitized, sampled or scored, and no useful product is established. Parent molecular evidence reports concentrated leading families, inconsistent functional-group context, reactive attachments, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereo. The closest current-Parent structural controls are contrary evidence: intact relocation n-14d23720adc5 makes 371 conserved identity-changing moves, 35 accepted descendants and five direct parent wins that all later breed, yet loses 0.03333581611976433 in mean. Ring construction n-870ed6964d46 supplies 179 evaluated noncopy descendants and 96 later breeders yet loses 0.04504628812412936. The ring/no-finishing combination n-6e3c92b5dcd0 has 169 evaluated noncopy descendants, complete immediate structural persistence and 103 later breeders, but loses 0.03400446507579402 despite its positive heterogeneous interaction. Finishing-only removal n-5a357a2ac96f loses 0.03624285568753934 despite more local parent wins. Thus useful source ranking, continuation and finishing remain intact while one new source-conserving arrangement route is tested. These observations motivate access, not a claim that conservation, diversity or reuse raises endpoints.
hypothesis: Add an optional single-source two-single-bond rewiring mode inside change_bond that replaces two vertex-disjoint nonaromatic single bonds by an alternative perfect matching of their four endpoints, conserving atom attributes, per-atom heavy degree, bond-order sum and molecular formula under the fixed selected-first-bond sampling law.

finding_summary.headline: Rewiring yields clean, reused improvements but lowers the complete-panel mean by 0.03953
finding_summary.insights: Lack of valid products, failed delivery and complete absence of productive reuse are ruled out as explanations for this route’s loss. Local improvements were real, but they were insufficient: over the whole search, parent wins rose from 629 to 709 while mean offspring score fell from 0.38526 to 0.35259 and the mean best-parent reference fell from 0.47046 to 0.42528. There were more incumbent improvements, but their summed magnitudes fell from 5.80766 to 5.21465. Thus easier parent comparisons and more reuse can coexist with worse endpoints. The chemical review likewise shows that alternative ring arrangements can retain reactive bonds and unresolved geometry or stereochemistry; conservation does not establish feasible or useful chemistry. Four unevaluated pool products also changed aromatic representation after passing the registered conservation witness, so exact attribute preservation cannot be extended across every canonical reparse. The complete result supports an adverse effect of adding this fixed route in this composition, including its displaced legacy opportunities and changed adaptive history. It does not identify a chemical mediator or the value of the whole graph-search foundation.
finding_summary.results: The route executed throughout the panel: 3,141 switches were sampled, 74 failed the sanitation conservation gate, and 3,067 passed, including 2,861 immediate identity changes. It supplied 178 evaluated offspring. Of 124 clean rewrites of a scored source, 26 beat that source and 24 of those winners later bred; one unused winner still had a later opportunity, while one was born in the final batch. Across all route offspring there were 38 wins, 32 ties and 108 losses, and 126 were actually reused. Nevertheless, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.556135, a complete paired loss of 0.039534 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed averages declined; four of fifteen endpoints improved and eleven declined. The standard deviation of seed averages fell from 0.026593 to 0.020758, which does not offset the lower score.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and amine-rich molecules explore new ring arrangements while retaining reactive bonds and unresolved geometry and stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: The output contains compact fused nitrogen heterocycles, linked aza-aromatics, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant: the digest ring-closure-string incidence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string incidence from 0.8575 to 0.977. These are incidences of SMILES text features among molecules, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 on every task, despite visible protonatable amines and potentially stereogenic centres. Synthetic plausibility is questionable and drug-likeness weak overall because recognizable medicinal chemistry coexists with N-halogen/O-halogen bonds, reactive peripheral groups and difficult ring arrangements. Diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with narrower families among a seed's leaders; the nonaromatic medium-ring family is a counterexample to universal aromatic convergence. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent search trajectory files were read, covering 9000 records; each Child task has 900 records including 870 optimizer proposals. No paths or task comparisons are missing. The immutable context reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 and no profile-mismatched seeds. The Parent's older same-code comparison had different profile conditions; that historical limitation does not negate the complete current pairing and supplies no component attribution. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not all seed incumbents. Sizes, bond environments and ring descriptions below were read from the supplied graphs with RDKit; perceived ring-basis sizes do not establish accessible conformations, stability or synthetic routes. The complete record-level audit and path hashes are in /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.slots/round-0024-slot-0/molecular_trajectory_audit.json. Topology contrasts concern observed accepted outputs. Trajectories alone do not join those structures to a particular edit, distinguish clean rewrites from mixed histories, or establish physical atom conservation, activation, reuse or chemical mediation. Conserved formula and degree would not by themselves certify useful functional arrangements or remove undesirable chemistry; route-specific conservation must be established separately. The transferable gaps retain the provenance recorded by the indexed Parent report and the conditions of this new observation.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 25 heavy atoms: an aromatic fused framework bearing methoxy, methyl and acetyl groups, an N-brominated diarylamine, and an additional fused four-membered N-N/C=N ring. Seed 1 instead reaches a 24-heavy-atom annulated imine/indole framework with methoxy groups and carbon-bound aryl fluorine; it has no N-halogen or O-halogen bond. The 25-heavy-atom seed-2 leader retains an indole carboxamide, but connects its ring nitrogen to an N-fluoro anilino group and carries a chloromethyl ether. The Parent leaders instead comprise an indole-associated cumulene, a pyridyl N-hydroxy amide, and an indole-aryl diketone. Thus the Child changes the leading annulation and linker arrangements while remaining in compact aromatic-rich chemistry. Indole amides, ketones and aryl ethers are recognizable synthetic motifs; the additional unsaturated small ring and N-halogen attachments make the strongest examples questionable targets.
liabilities: N-Br on a diarylamine and N-F on an N-N-linked anilino group have different reactivity from ordinary aryl C-Br or C-F; the chloromethyl ether is another potentially labile environment.
The fused four-membered N-N/C=N ring raises strain and electronic-structure concerns. Annulation and aromatic notation are not evidence of isolability.
Large linked derivatives and tiny inorganic fragments are still evaluated even though their observed scores are negligible.
missing_features: The best seed-0 and seed-2 examples do not demonstrate comparably rewarded conventional nitrogen substitution while retaining their favorable aromatic/polar organization; the seed-1 leader is a real counterexample to any claim that such chemistry is wholly absent.
Accessible geometry and electronic structure of the extra fused unsaturated four-membered ring are not established by its valid SMILES.
The trajectories do not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore or a universal requirement for an amide, a particular halogen, or additional rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 fused N-bromo ketone reaches 0.48660033404583897, whereas a much larger linked indole/amidine/peroxide structure at seed 1 evaluation 21 scores 2.560108286557955e-18 and ClBr scores 0.0. This associates reward with a compact combined aromatic/polar arrangement, not merely more atoms or halogens. The otherwise matching N-fluoro and N-bromo acetylindoles at seed 0 evaluations 245 and 273 both score 0.438122145211641; this tie does not establish that either reactive N-halogen bond is needed. The N/O-halogen-free seed-1 leader reaches 0.40018522659086975. In seed order 0, 1, 2 the Child best observed scores are 0.48660033404583897, 0.40018522659086975, 0.46092619585962435; the matched published Parent values are 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596, 0.438972502037081. The opposite seed-1 direction prevents interpreting the changed topologies as uniformly favorable.

per_task.generated_character: The 36-heavy-atom seed-0 leader links a pyrrole and two pyridyl regions through aryl-N and amino connections. It bears ethyl, carbon-bound fluorine/chlorofluoromethyl, methoxymethyl, carbonyl and formyl groups, including an aryl-O-N linkage; its tied analogue substitutes S for that linking O. Seed 1 reaches a smaller 28-heavy-atom fused nitrogen-rich dione linked to a fluorinated pyridine through a chlorinated carbon between nitrogens, with N-methoxy substitution. Seed 2 instead expands to a 54-heavy-atom, three-benzene thioether/carbonyl-imine assembly with alkenyl appendages, N-F and O-F groups. The Parent seed-0 leader is a more compact linked fused/bridged nitrogen-carbonyl-thione framework; it is not reproduced by merely enlarging the Child's aromatic assembly. Some heteroaryl connections and amide alternatives are conventional synthetic motifs, but the heteroatom linkages, chlorinated aminal-like centre and large multiply reactive assemblies limit confidence in practical synthesis.
liabilities: Aryl-O-N, S-N, N-methoxy and chlorinated aminal-like linkages need environment-specific stability assessment; these are not equivalent to ordinary aryl ethers or simple tertiary amines.
The seed-2 leader contains imine N-F and aryl O-F bonds, multiple unsaturated substituents and a large sulfur-containing aromatic assembly; a score does not establish stable solution chemistry.
The observed 0.5 floor for very small fragments is not a chemical quality endorsement.
missing_features: The Child does not recover the Parent's strongly rewarded compact heterocyclic organization across these seeds, despite already producing many rings and heteroatoms; no exact missing motif can be inferred from these nonmatched structures.
Consistent access to less reactive peripheral substitutions at similar scores is not established across seeds, although the near-tied propionamide is a useful existing counterexample.
The chlorinated carbon linking nitrogens has unspecified stereochemical identity, and the large seed-2 assemblies lack demonstrated useful conformational organization.

The O-N- and S-N-linked seed-0 leaders both score 0.6162862621389249. A propionamide alternative without either of those linkages reaches 0.6162107462296794, so the unusual O-N/S-N connection is not demonstrated to be essential. per_task.generated_character: Substantial aromatic surface is combined with accessible aliphatic amines. The 29-heavy-atom seed-2 leader contains two halogenated phenyl rings, a tertiary azetidine, an amino/ether-substituted carbon and an N-chloro aniline. A nearly tied seed-2 molecule instead contains an enlarged nitrogen ring and a bridged carbocyclic/aryl region without N-halogen or O-halogen bonds. Seed 1 yields a 28-heavy-atom biaryl phenol bearing a secondary alkylamine and a substituted aziridine with a bromomethyl appendage. Its late piperidine-containing product provides a less strained saturated-amine counterexample. Seed 0 produces a 32-heavy-atom flexible diaryl system with tertiary and primary amines, sulfinamide, thiol and bromomethyl groups. The Parent already reaches flexible tertiary aryl amines and conventional pyrrolidine-containing aryl systems, so amine or ring access is not new. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry arrangements, with specific reactive bonds, small-ring strain and stereochemical uncertainty rather than a complete absence of plausible synthetic handles.
liabilities: The seed-1 aziridine and bromomethyl substituent present strain and electrophilic-reactivity concerns; the seed-2 N-chloro aniline is separate reactive chemistry.
The seed-0 flexible leader contains a potentially reactive bromomethyl group, thiol and configurationally unresolved sulfinamide environment in addition to its amines.
Bridged and substituted cyclic products have multiple unspecified stereogenic environments; a sanitized molecular graph does not establish a feasible conformer.
missing_features: Basic amine centres are already present; the missing capability is consistent placement of those centres and aromatic regions in less reactive, stereochemically defined structures, rather than adding a named amine scaffold.
Substituted small-ring and bridged centres lack assigned stereochemistry, and neutral SMILES do not determine the relevant protonation states.
The scores do not establish that an N-Cl bond, an aziridine, a bromomethyl group or any exact missing receptor motif is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-chloro azetidine leader scores 0.9999925346021972 and the N/O-halogen-free enlarged-ring alternative scores 0.9999915582910128. Seed 1 also reaches 0.9852733144472993 with a late piperidine/biaryl amine lacking N-halogen, O-halogen and bromomethyl groups. By contrast, an acylated and N-sulfonylated pyrrolidine with a sulfur/carboxyl appendage scores 0.0003556511895523401; the much smaller aryl sulfinamide scores 0.0008152422078592413, and a late pentyl bromobenzene lacking amines scores 0.004368742491675696. The visible association is the combined arrangement of aromatic regions and available aliphatic nitrogen, not halogen loading, one particular ring size, or sulfinamide alone. In seed order 0, 1, 2 the Child best observed scores are 0.9821095872557019, 0.9955839096050136, 0.9999925346021972; the matched published Parent values are 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906, 0.9999934235240012. Near-ceiling returned scores do not measure stability, receptor selectivity or experimentally verified binding.

per_task.generated_character: The 33-heavy-atom seed-0 leader combines pyridyl and phenyl aromatic regions with a densely bridged nitrogen framework, a cyclic dicarbonyl segment, propyl and ethoxy substituents. Its perceived ring basis includes several medium rings; this is real topology complexity, not merely an aromatic side-chain series. Seed 1 reaches another 33-heavy-atom diaryl nitrogen/carbonyl system with an eleven-membered ring in its perceived ring basis. Seed 2 retains a 34-heavy-atom quinoline attached to a seven-membered N-N-containing lactam and a separate oxygen/nitrogen dicarbonyl ring. The Parent already generates diaryl bridged lactams and quinoline-linked nitrogen-dicarbonyl systems; the Child changes bridges and ring segmentation within related functional chemistry. Amides, lactams and aza-aromatics are recognizable, but crowded bridge geometry, medium-ring closure and stereochemical control make these specific structures challenging synthetic propositions.
liabilities: Dense bridges and unsaturated ring junctions may impose difficult geometry; feasibility cannot be certified from ring-basis counts or canonical SMILES.
Some alternatives introduce N-N or N-O functionality, whose behavior depends on its carbonyl and ring environment rather than heteroatom count alone.
Potential stereogenic saturated bridge centres remain unassigned throughout these families.
missing_features: Simpler, geometrically credible alternatives retaining the rewarded aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization are not consistently demonstrated among the leaders.
The bridged and medium-ring products lack defined stereochemical and conformational identity; conventional functional groups alone do not supply it.
The trajectories do not identify an exact absent target motif, and already-rich ring chemistry contradicts a general need for more rings.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in the indexed n-62daf219c70a Molecular report; it is re-observed here in n-1e99f8383153 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, at 300 observations per task and batch size 10, against the complete current-profile Parent panel. Leaders retain N-Br on diarylamine, N-F on heterocycles or imines, N-Cl on aniline, O-F, chloromethyl ether and bromomethyl environments. Counterexamples include a strong fused fluorophenol/imino-carbonyl molecule without N/O-halogen bonds, a nearly tied propionamide alternative, and high-scoring conventional saturated cyclic amines. The issue is environment-specific, not lack of amines, rings or ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently offer conventional bond environments while retaining otherwise favorable aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations would need access to plausible local substitutions and linkages that preserve useful arrangements learned from real feedback. Conservation of atom inventory or degree does not guarantee benign functional chemistry and may leave undesirable features elsewhere in a molecule. These output associations neither attribute the liability to a particular component nor establish that a universal reactive-group filter improves scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in the indexed n-62daf219c70a Molecular report; it is re-observed here in n-1e99f8383153 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, at 300 observations per task and batch size 10, against the complete current-profile Parent panel. Accepted leaders include a fused four-membered N-N/C=N ring, multiply bridged nitrogen-carbonyl frameworks and an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring. Other accepted outputs contain ordinary saturated cyclic amines and recognizable fused carbonyl rings. The presence of those plausible motifs is a counterexample to blanket ring implausibility; changing topology is already possible, but its feasible geometry is unresolved.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can change ring connectivity without establishing a geometrically credible complete ring system.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need feasible alternatives sensitive to ring closure geometry, unsaturation and bridge connectivity while retaining useful functional relationships. Ring incidence, formula conservation and sanitation alone cannot provide that information. This motivates assessing feasibility, not banning ring formation or claiming that the registered rewiring route produced any particular structure without an indexed execution-to-trajectory join.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in the indexed n-62daf219c70a Molecular report; it is re-observed here in n-1e99f8383153 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, at 300 observations per task and batch size 10, against the complete current-profile Parent panel. Every supplied task digest has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. The cited substituted azetidine/aziridine, cyclopropyl, chlorinated heteroatom-linked carbon and bridged lactam structures visibly admit stereochemical questions. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but protonatable amines are present; uncharged serialization is not evidence that basic chemistry is absent.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not resolve stereochemical identity after producing potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and graph transformations would need to preserve or explicitly resolve relevant stereochemistry, distinguishing configurationally stable centres from achiral or rapidly interconverting cases. Protonation and tautomerism need separate assessment. These records show unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty, newly caused stereo loss, or a component-specific failure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in the indexed n-62daf219c70a Molecular report; it is re-observed here in n-1e99f8383153 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, at 300 observations per task and batch size 10, against the complete current-profile Parent panel. Tiny halogen, hydrocarbon and inorganic proposals remain at observed low scores, while oversized linked aromatic products can also score very poorly. An observed close pair retains a fluorinated cyclopropyl/imino-carbonyl framework but loses a hydroxyl oxygen: the returned score changes from 0.5765242212490009 to 0.049171789152450435. Near-tied amide-linker variants and smaller high-scoring cyclic amines show that simplification and conventional alternatives can also preserve useful context.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain favorable functional-group context during simplification, fragmentation or elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need context-preserving transformations informed by its own accepted feedback, with alternatives that replace or simplify dispensable parts without assuming that more atoms, more heteroatoms or more rings are better. No fixed size threshold or universal protected pharmacophore follows from these conditional observations, and no source/product edit attribution is supplied by a close molecular pair alone.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was originally recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained in the indexed n-62daf219c70a Molecular report; it is re-observed here in n-1e99f8383153 on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, at 300 observations per task and batch size 10, against the complete current-profile Parent panel. Leaders repeatedly vary halogen placement, small substituents, carbonyl-adjacent nitrogen and ring junctions on retained fused heteroaromatic, aryl-amine and nitrogen-dicarbonyl families. Distinct seeds do reach different cores, including a nonaromatic medium-ring family; rich ring incidence and those alternative cores contradict global scaffold collapse. Complete paired observations contain contrary seed directions, so newly encountered topology is not automatically useful coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically independent plausible alternatives to each leading family are not consistently represented among a seed's strongest outputs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The relevant capability is access to chemically distinct, feasible complete arrangements preserving relationships supported by task-local feedback. Distinct SMILES or added bridges alone do not demonstrate that capability. These chemistry associations do not identify which search component limits coverage, do not establish a benefit from greater diversity, and do not authorize a task-specific scaffold source.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
